# The PCB golden rules

Every rule this project holds a board to, with its authority, its applicability, how it is verified and what
its verification is currently worth. Generated from the registry: the registry is the authority and this page
is its rendering.

Registry version **2026-09-16.1**, fingerprint **a453bedd2b5ad14d**, 56 rules over 34 domains.

## How to read a rule

`BLOCKER` stops a release, `MUST_JUSTIFY` needs a written reason, `ADVISORY` informs. `SOURCE_UNVERIFIED`
means the limit's authority is not on file, which is not the same as the rule being wrong: it means nobody
can check it. A `HEURISTIC` may never be a blocker; where one is doing a blocker's work today it is written
as a screen under the principle it screens for.

## Product Envelope

### ENV-001  operating envelope declared

The product's electrical envelope, environmental limits, operating modes, expected life and foreseeable
misuse are written down and dated, and every derating, spacing, thermal and reliability rule resolves its
numbers against that declaration rather than against an assumption.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY, RELIABILITY, DOCUMENTATION |
| verified by | MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | NONE_YET |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** A dated envelope document exists naming, at minimum: ambient temperature range in use and in storage,
humidity and ingress expectation, altitude, vibration and shock expectation, input voltage ranges, the
defined operating modes, and the single-fault conditions the design is expected to survive. Every rule in
this registry whose limit depends on one of those numbers cites it.

**Why** Derating, creepage, current capacity and thermal limits are all functions of the envelope. Without a declared
envelope each rule silently picks its own, and two rules can then contradict each other while both look
satisfied.

**If violated** A board qualified at a bench temperature fails in a vehicle in summer; a spacing chosen for pollution degree
2 sits in a kit carried through rain.

**Today** no envelope document exists: temperature, humidity, altitude, vibration and single-fault assumptions are
unwritten, and every derating rule resolves against nothing

### ENV-002  no claim without a test

No environmental or protection rating is claimed in any public or shipped document unless the test that
establishes it has been run and recorded.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | DOCUMENTATION, SAFETY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, MANUAL_REVIEW at RELEASE_PACKAGE (partially automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | claims_check.py plus claims-allow.txt, one declared exemption per line with its reason |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** Every rating word in README, BUILD, ASSEMBLY, the release notes and the order paperwork is either accompanied
by the test record that establishes it, or is written as an intent ("designed to", "untested").

**Why** An ingress or environmental claim is a promise to whoever carries the kit.

**If violated** A kit is trusted in conditions nobody tested it in.

**Today** 16 September 2026: a screen over the eight public documents, in final_gate.py because the release package is
a set of documents as much as a set of folders and they reach the public mirror within minutes. It finds the
sentences that assert a rating or a capability and asks each for a qualifier, an evidence reference, a
negation, or a declared reason. The distinction it holds: a rating attached to a part the project BUYS is the
maker's own claim and quoting it is a fact about the bill of materials, while the same rating attached to
THIS KIT is a promise about hardware that has never been built. Nine vendor ratings are declared with their
reason; 19 claim sentences, 0 unqualified

## Schematic Integrity

### SCH-001  ERC clean or explained

The schematic passes electrical rule checking with no error-severity violation that is not individually
explained in writing.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | ERC at SCHEMATIC (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_sch_*.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one violation on one board, expires the next schematic regeneration |

**Accept when** Zero error-severity ERC violations, or each one covered by an allow entry carrying a reason.

**Why** An unconnected or conflicting pin is the cheapest defect to find and the most expensive to find later.

**If violated** A driver contention or a floating enable ships.

**Today** an allow line without a reason waves nothing through, proved by fixture

### SCH-002  board matches its netlist

The board being judged is the board that was placed from the schematic being shipped: every component, every
net and every pin connection agrees between the netlist and the board file.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION, DOCUMENTATION |
| verified by | SCRIPT at PLACED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_pcb_*3.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** Three comparisons, each with its denominator: every netlist component is on the board, every board footprint
carrying a net is in the netlist, and every net's pin set agrees. KiCad's synthetic unconnected-pin
placeholders are not nets on either side.

**Why** A stale netlist makes every downstream gate judge a design nobody is building. It has happened here: a
comment swallowed three resistors and the board placed, routed and passed every gate three parts short.

**If violated** A board is fabricated from a schematic that no longer describes it.

**Today** three comparisons with denominators; runs on the placed and on the routed board

### SCH-003  cross-board contracts

Every signal that leaves one board and arrives on another agrees at both ends: pin for pin on the connector,
in name, in direction, and in the number of drivers.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, e5, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION, SAFETY |
| verified by | SCRIPT at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_sch_*.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** Every declared contract passes on the netlists of the boards in the manifest; a board whose netlist is absent
makes the check INCONCLUSIVE, never passing.

**Why** No single-board gate can see a contract. The EMCON line was once wired as a ring oscillator with its polarity
inverted between two boards, and each board's own gate passed.

**If violated** Asserting a safety line enables the thing it is meant to inhibit.

**Today** INCONCLUSIVE when a sibling netlist is absent, which is correct; the contracts themselves are a hand-written
list and their completeness is not itself checked

### SCH-004  a safety line fails safe

Every line whose assertion inhibits a hazard (transmit inhibit, zeroize, shore inhibit, kill) is designed so
that a disconnected cable, an unpowered board or a missing module leaves the system in the safe state.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | SCRIPT, MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_sch_b.py, gen_sch_c.py, gen_sch_d.py |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** For each such line: the pull direction, the driver count and the behaviour with the far board absent are
stated and verified on the netlist; the safe state is the unpowered state.

**Why** A hardware inhibit that depends on a cable being present is not an inhibit.

**If violated** The panel is unplugged and the transmitter is enabled; or ZEROIZE is asserted and nothing wipes, which is the
state recorded in the 9 September review and still open.

**Today** the transmit-inhibit chain is checked; ZEROIZE has NO hardware path at all (the secure element carries power
and I2C only) and the shore-inhibit and kill lines are not checked for fail-safe direction

## Component Selection

### CMP-001  absolute maximum never reached

No component is operated at or above any absolute maximum rating of its datasheet under any declared
operating mode, including startup, shutdown, hot-plug and the single-fault conditions the envelope names.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | COMPONENT_REQUIREMENT |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY, RELIABILITY, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | SCRIPT, MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | NONE_YET |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** For every part on a net whose nominal voltage exceeds 80 percent of the part's rating, and for every part in
a current path above 1 A, a recorded comparison of the applied stress against the datasheet maximum, citing
the datasheet page. Capacitor DC bias derating is applied to every MLCC used for energy storage or filtering.

**Why** A 50 V capacitor on a 54 V output is not a margin question, it is a wrong part; the tree carried exactly that
on the PoE stage until owner ruling 10.

**If violated** A part fails short on the bench or in the field, often taking the stage with it.

**Today** no derating or absolute-maximum comparison exists anywhere; the 22 uF 50 V part on a 54 V output was found by
a person, not by a check

### CMP-002  the package on the land is the package ordered

Every part's ordered package matches the land pattern it is placed on.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | COMPONENT_REQUIREMENT |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | ASSEMBLY, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION, SUPPLY_CHAIN |
| verified by | SCRIPT, VENDOR_CONFIRMATION at RELEASE_PACKAGE (automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | lcsc_fill.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one designator on one board, expires the next BOM export |

**Accept when** Every BOM row's ordering code is checked against the supplier's own record for package, and the package
agrees with the footprint the board places, with the check dated.

**Why** A TSSOP-38 order code sat on a QFN-38 land here, and a footprint key in a generator is a claim about a
package that nothing checked for four board phases.

**If violated** The assembler places a part that cannot solder to the land, or solders a wrong die.

**Today** package mismatch is caught against the supplier's own record, with a date

## Lifecycle Supply

### SUP-001  every placed part is buyable

Every part the assembler is asked to place is available in the quantity the order needs, at the time of the
order, or is declared hand-fitted with a written purchase route.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SUPPLY_CHAIN, ASSEMBLY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, VENDOR_CONFIRMATION at RELEASE_PACKAGE (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | lcsc_fill.py, jlc-handfit.txt |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one part, expires the order |

**Accept when** Every BOM row is CERTIFIED against the supplier's live catalogue with its stock at a recorded date, or
HAND_FIT with a route, or BENCH_FITTED and excluded from the placement file.

**Why** Stock of three against a need of five is a schedule risk that must be seen before the order, not after.

**If violated** An order is placed that cannot be assembled.

**Today** stock is read at a date; the date is the evidence's freshness

## Power Tree

### PWR-001  every rail is declared with its loads

Every rail on the board is declared with its nominal voltage, its typical and peak current, its source, its
drop budget and the loads that draw it; a rail that exists in copper and not in the declaration is a rail
nothing judges.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | POWER_INTEGRITY, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | SCRIPT at SCHEMATIC (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_sch_*.py via intent.rail() |
| maturity | **GENERATED_ONLY** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one rail, expires the next schematic regeneration |

**Accept when** The count of rails in the board's intent declaration equals the count of distinct power nets carrying more
than a declared threshold current on the board, and every declared rail names where its current goes.

**Why** The drop and density checks judge only declared rails. B's per-slot cores and E's downstream rails carry no
declaration today, so nothing has ever measured them.

**If violated** A rail droops or overheats and no check ever looked at it.

**Today** the check confirms a DECLARED rail exists on the board; nothing compares the declared set against the power
nets the board actually carries, and B's per-slot cores and E's downstream rails are undeclared

### PWR-002  sequencing and inrush

The order in which rails come up and go down is defined, and every rail's inrush, hot-plug and back-powering
behaviour is bounded by design rather than by luck.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | COMPONENT_REQUIREMENT |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION, RELIABILITY, SAFETY |
| verified by | MANUAL_REVIEW, SIMULATION at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_sch_a.py, gen_sch_b.py |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one rail, expires prototype validation |

**Accept when** A written sequencing statement per board naming, for each rail, what enables it, what it depends on, the
inrush limit and the device requirement it satisfies (for example a module's rail-order requirement).

**Why** Modules with multiple supplies latch up or brown out when their rails arrive in the wrong order.

**If violated** A module fails to boot intermittently, or draws current through a protection diode at startup.

**Today** sequencing exists in the design (LTC2954, enables, eFuses) and is written nowhere as a requirement with a
check

### PWR-003  protection coordination

Every fuse, eFuse, ideal diode and protection device is coordinated with what it protects: the clearing
characteristic sits below the damage characteristic of the weakest element downstream and above the worst
legitimate current.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, e, e5, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY, RELIABILITY |
| verified by | CALCULATION, MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_sch_a.py, gen_sch_e.py, gen_sch_p.py |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** For each protective element: the rated and peak current of the path, the element's rating and clearing curve
reference, the fault current available at that point, and the element downstream it is protecting.

**Why** Four boards sit on one energy chain from the cells with two 25 A blades on it; a fuse that never opens before
the conductor does is decoration.

**If violated** A short in the kit is cleared by a track or a connector instead of by the fuse.

**Today** two 25 A blades, three 10 A blades, eFuses and an ideal diode, and no coordination study: no fuse curve is on
file

## Decoupling

### DEC-001  decoupling loop area

Every decoupling capacitor forms a loop with the pin it serves and its return that is small enough for the
frequencies that pin's current actually contains.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | POWER_INTEGRITY, EMC, SIGNAL_INTEGRITY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION at PLACED_BOARD (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | bypass_slots.py, bypass_place.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one capacitor, expires the next placement |

**Accept when** Each declared decoupling entry states its pin, its distance, its via count and the loop it forms; an entry
beyond the declared distance carries a written reason. The distance itself is derived per device from the
current's spectral content, not taken as one project-wide number.

**Why** Loop inductance, not capacitance, decides high-frequency decoupling. The project's present 3 mm number is a
heuristic and is recorded as one.

**If violated** Rail collapse at switching edges, radiated emissions, and marginal digital timing.

**Today** the 3 mm distance is a project number applied to every device; the loop inductance it stands for is never
computed, and a board declares exceptions in an allow file

## Power Integrity

### PI-001  conductor current capacity

Every conductor carrying a rail's current is wide enough, in the copper weight it is actually built in, to
carry that current within the temperature rise the envelope allows, judged on the narrowest piece of copper
that carries a meaningful share of the current.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | STANDARD |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY, THERMAL, RELIABILITY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| | IPC-2221 generic standard on printed board design, current-carrying capacity charts, IPC, current capacity charts -- NOT IN THIS TREE |
| | IPC-2152 standard for determining current-carrying capacity, IPC -- NOT IN THIS TREE |
| implementation | power_copper.py, gen_pcb_*3.py bands |
| maturity | **SOURCE_UNVERIFIED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** For every declared rail: the narrowest conductor carrying above a declared share of the rail current, its
cross-section computed from the board's own stackup copper weight, and the resulting temperature rise against
the envelope's limit. The limit and the standard edition are cited.

**Why** The project's density check was lenient by up to 98 percent for two weeks and twelve rails on four boards
exceeded the published limit while every one read MET, because the verdict was taken on voltage drop.

**If violated** A track runs hot, its resin degrades, and the failure is progressive rather than sudden.

**Today** the conductor measure is implemented and tested; its limit comes from a formula in a code comment, no IPC
document is in the tree, and IPC-2152 has never been considered. 16 September 2026: it reads its OWN verdict
now (dc_density). One verdict served both power rules, so a density miss failed the board through the drop
rule and a limit with no source decided a board through a rule that has one. Board A read MISSED VBAT 0.38
percent of 14.4 V, which looks like a voltage failure and is a density one

### PI-002  rail voltage drop

Every rail arrives at its loads inside the drop budget declared for it.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | POWER_INTEGRITY, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | power_copper.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one rail on one board, expires prototype measurement |

**Accept when** A resistive solve of the filled board from source pad to every load pad at the declared peak current,
reported as millivolts and as a percentage against the rail's own budget, with the solver's residual checked
before the number is read.

**Why** A rail that droops at peak is a brown-out that only appears under load.

**If violated** A module resets when a transmitter keys.

**Today** the solver's residual is checked before the number is read. Since 16 September the dc_drop verdict carries
the VOLTAGE DROP alone, against each rail's own budget, and the current capacity is a separate verdict under
PI-001

### PI-003  via current capacity

Every via carrying rail current is counted and rated: the number of vias at a layer transition carries the
rail's peak current within the same temperature rise the conductor rule allows.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | STANDARD |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | THERMAL, RELIABILITY, SAFETY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | prefanout.py, gen_pcb_*3.py stitch vias |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one transition, expires the next route |

**Accept when** For each rail transition: via count, barrel cross-section from the plating thickness the fabricator quotes,
current per via and the total against the rail's peak.

**Why** A 0.4 mm barrel carries about an ampere; a 10 A rail crossing on three vias is a heater.

**If violated** Barrel cracking and progressive resistance rise at the transition.

**Today** via current capacity is asserted in generator comments and measured by nothing

## Grounding Shielding

### GND-001  one deliberate ground system

The board's ground system is deliberate: every partition, moat or separate ground is there for a written
reason, and every conductor crossing between them does so at a defined point.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | EMC, SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, SAFETY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, MANUAL_REVIEW at ROUTED_BOARD (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_pcb_*3.py pours |
| maturity | **GENERATED_ONLY** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one board, expires the next placement |

**Accept when** Either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing
points named and the signals that cross listed.

**Why** An accidental split is the commonest cause of a return path taking the long way round.

**If violated** Radiated emissions, coupled noise into analogue nodes, and common-mode current on cables.

**Today** phantom-net pours are refused and pour coverage is measured; no check asks whether a partition is deliberate
or where a crossing happens

### GND-002  chassis and cable-shield strategy

How signal ground meets the metal of the enclosure, and what happens to every cable shield entering or
leaving the kit, is decided once and implemented the same way everywhere.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, e |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | EMC, SAFETY |
| verified by | MANUAL_REVIEW at PLACED_BOARD (human or lab only) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_pcb_c3.py standoffs |
| maturity | **DOCUMENTED_ONLY** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope the kit, expires pre-compliance testing |

**Accept when** A written chassis-bond statement: which points bond, through what impedance, and the intended path for
electrostatic discharge and for cable-borne common-mode current.

**Why** Eleven coaxial jacks and a metal face plate make the enclosure part of the circuit whether it is designed or
not.

**If violated** Discharge current finds a path through a signal return; the kit fails an ESD test at a connector.

**Today** eight standoffs bond C's ground to the plate; no chassis-bond or shield strategy is written for the kit

## Stackup

### STK-001  the stackup is declared, feasible and in the board

The board file carries the stackup it will be built on, that stackup is one the chosen fabricator builds, and
every impedance, current and spacing rule resolves against it rather than against a default.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | FAB_LIMIT |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | FABRICATION, SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, POWER_INTEGRITY |
| verified by | SCRIPT, VENDOR_CONFIRMATION at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| | fabricator PCB capability page, the selected fabricator -- v2/vendor/seals/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-page.txt |
| implementation | stackup_write.py |
| maturity | **SOURCE_UNVERIFIED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** The board's copper layer count, thickness, per-layer copper weight and dielectric constants are present in
the board file and match a named, dated fabricator stackup; the order paperwork names the same one.

**Why** Every impedance and current number is a function of the stack; an unstated stack makes them all unfounded.

**If violated** Boards arrive on a different stack and the controlled impedances are wrong.

**Today** the stackup is written into the board and read back by the impedance check; the fabricator capability file in
the tree is an empty JavaScript page and nothing reads it

Every board's layer count carries its own written decision: the measurement that forced it and the cost it

**Accept when** For each board: a dated decision naming the measurement (a route at the lower count, or a requirement the

**Why** Four layers entered this project as a first board's default and was copied; two promotions to six were

**Today** layer_judge measures what the router did, not what the board needs, and says so; no like-for-like price for

## Return Path

### RET-001  a continuous adjacent return path

Every signal's return current has a continuous, low-impedance path adjacent to its outgoing conductor for the
whole of the conductor's length, adequate for the spectral content that signal's edge rate produces. Adequacy
is judged from edge rate, electrical length, the reference structures the signal actually runs over, the
discontinuities it crosses and the interface's own requirement, not from a single geometric proxy.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION, MANUAL_REVIEW at ROUTED_BOARD (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | signal_class.py plus each board's signal_classes table, judged by intent_checks.py |
| maturity | **GENERATED_ONLY** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one net class on one board, expires prototype EMC measurement |

**Accept when** Every signal net is classified by edge rate and electrical length. For each class, the adequacy criterion is
stated (for a fast edge: an uninterrupted reference plane on an adjacent layer for the length of the run,
with every reference change accompanied by a return transition; for a slow edge: a return path whose loop
area is bounded). Each net is then judged against its own class's criterion, with the classification
recorded.

**Why** Return current flows under its conductor at high frequency and takes the lowest-resistance path at low
frequency. What must be continuous is the RETURN, and what makes a discontinuity matter is the current's
spectrum, not the existence of copper on a neighbouring layer.

**If violated** Radiated emission from an enlarged loop, crosstalk into neighbouring nets, reflections at the discontinuity,
and common-mode conversion on differential pairs.

**Today** 16 September 2026: the principle is implemented and the heuristic is no longer standing in for it. Every net
gets a spectral-content class from EVIDENCE (the board's own impedance-targeted net class, or a declaration
in boards/<letter>.json carrying a written basis naming the part or interface that decides it), and each
class is asked the question it deserves: a fast net for an ADJACENT reference within a tolerance, a slow one
for whether a return path EXISTS at all. Four properties keep a relaxation from becoming an exemption
mechanism, each with a rule: a declaration without a reason is refused, an unclassified net is judged at the
STRICTEST bar and named, a declaration cannot downgrade a net the board itself calls impedance-targeted, and
the relaxed class asks a different QUESTION rather than a looser number. It is GENERATED_ONLY and not
ENFORCED for one reason and it is the honest one: THE PER-CLASS TOLERANCES ARE THIS PROJECT'S OWN NUMBERS,
not a standard's. The 10 mm or 5 percent of the fast classes is the 15 September ruling's figure calibrated
on board A's anti-pad rows; the 30 mm or 15 percent of CLOCKED_DIGITAL is a judgement. Until a source backs
them, they are a written screen and say so

### RET-002  plane-adjacency screen

As a screening test for RET-001, the fraction of each signal net's track length that has no filled reference
zone on an adjacent layer is measured and reported, and a net above the screening threshold is examined
against RET-001 rather than failed outright.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | HEURISTIC |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | SCRIPT at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gen_pcb_*3.py pours |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one net, expires the next route |

**Accept when** The screen reports, per net: total track length, uncovered length, the runs that make it up, and what sits on
the neighbouring layers at each run. The present threshold, the larger of 10 mm or 5 percent, is a
calibration against one board's measured behaviour and is recorded as such, not as a limit from an authority.

**Why** The screen is cheap, mechanical and finds real discontinuities. It is not a law: it counts a net's own via
anti-pads as uncovered, which is how D and E read 11 and 9 nets over while their reference structure is
continuous everywhere a signal actually runs.

**If violated** Used as a law it refuses good boards (false positives at every via) and passes bad ones (a covered net whose
reference changes layer with no return transition).

**Today** 16 September 2026: it no longer stands in for RET-001. The same measurement runs, and what it is compared
against now depends on the net's declared spectral class, so the screen is a screen again. It still counts a
net's own via anti-pads as uncovered, which is what RET-003 is about and is why boards D and E read what they
read

### RET-003  return transition at a reference change

Where a signal changes layer and its reference conductor changes with it, a return path for that transition
exists: a via between the two reference conductors when they are different nets at the same potential, a
stitching capacitor when they are different potentials, or no transition at all.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | SCRIPT, CALCULATION at ROUTED_BOARD (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | NONE_YET |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one class of transition on one board, expires prototype EMC measurement |

**Accept when** For each signal via, the reference conductor before and after the transition is determined. A transition that
does not change the reference needs nothing. A transition that changes it carries a return path whose form is
stated and whose position is close enough for the signal's spectral content.

**Why** The discontinuity is the reference CHANGE, not the via. A via between two layers that share one reference
plane needs no companion; a via that moves a signal from one plane's field to another's does.

**If violated** The return current detours around the anti-pad or through a decoupling capacitor, enlarging the loop.

**Today** nothing determines the reference conductor before and after a transition; return_via's same-plane exemption
is the nearest thing and is a geometric approximation of it

### RET-004  ground-via proximity screen

As a screening test for RET-003, every signal via outside a fine-pitch escape fan is measured for the
distance to the nearest ground via, and a via beyond the screening distance is examined against RET-003
rather than failed outright.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | HEURISTIC |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | SCRIPT at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | gnd_grid.py, return_via.py fixer |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one via, expires the next route |

**Accept when** The screen reports signal vias judged, vias exempt with the reason, vias satisfied, and vias lacking with
their positions and nets. The present 1.5 mm distance and the 0.5 mm fine-pitch exemption are project
calibrations and are recorded as such.

**Why** Ground vias beside a transition are the usual implementation of RET-003 and are cheap to place before a
route. The distance that matters follows from the signal's spectrum and the via field geometry, not from one
number.

**If violated** Used as a law it demands vias where the reference never changed, and it says nothing about a transition that
has a via at the wrong potential.

**Today** 1.5 mm and the 0.5 mm fan exemption are project calibrations; the grid makes the screen pass by construction
on D, and costs E its route

Every net whose interface specifies a characteristic impedance is routed in a geometry that achieves it on
the board's own stackup, the target and tolerance are stated to the fabricator, and the fabricator confirms
it can build and test it.

| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one class on one board, expires prototype measurement |

**Accept when** Per controlled class: the target, the tolerance, the geometry as built, the computed impedance from the
board's own stackup, a second opinion from a field solver where the closed form is known to be weak, and the
fabricator's written confirmation with a coupon where the tolerance demands it.

**Why** The closed forms and the 2D solver in this tree disagree by 38 percent on the stripline case and only one
solved point exists, so an impedance claimed from the closed form alone is not yet a claim.

**If violated** Reflections, failed compliance testing, and a link that works on the bench and not in the field.

**Today** closed forms from a standard not in the tree; the 2D solver disagrees by 38 percent on the stripline case
with one solved point; no fabricator confirmation and no coupon

from the table now and full.sh blocks the placed board on class_floor.py

## Differential Pairs

### PAIR-001  a pair is coupled and matched

A differential pair is routed as a pair: the two conductors run together at the geometry its target demands,
their lengths match inside the budget the interface allows, and both ends of the pair are symmetrical.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | INTERFACE_REQUIREMENT |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, d |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | SCRIPT at ROUTED_BOARD (automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | pair_preroute.py, meander.py |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope one class on one board, expires prototype measurement |

**Accept when** Per pair: the coupled length as a fraction of the judged length, the intra-pair length difference against the
interface's own skew budget, and the via and station symmetry. The project's present 1 mm gate is a project
decision, and the interface's own budget is cited beside it.

**Why** An uncoupled pair is two single-ended nets with the wrong impedance and a common-mode current.

**If violated** Common-mode conversion, radiated emission at the pair's own rate, and link errors.

**Today** coupling and the 1 mm length gate are enforced; the 1 mm is a project number and the interface's own skew
budget is not cited beside it

## Signal Integrity

### SI-001  transmission-line classification

Every net is classified by whether it behaves as a transmission line, from its rise time, propagation delay
and electrical length, and its topology and termination follow from that classification, not from its bit
rate or clock frequency.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | SIGNAL_INTEGRITY, EMC |
| verified by | CALCULATION, MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | NONE_YET |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by SESSION, scope one net class, expires prototype measurement |

**Accept when** A per-board table: net class, driver edge rate from the device datasheet, the length above which that edge
rate makes the net a transmission line on this stackup, and the nets that exceed it with their topology and
termination.

**Why** A 100 kHz bus with a 1 ns edge is a transmission line; a 10 MHz clock with a 20 ns edge over 30 mm is not.
Frequency alone decides nothing.

**If violated** Overshoot into a protection diode, double-clocking, and emissions from an unterminated stub.

**Today** no net in this project has ever been classified by edge rate; every impedance and return decision rests on
that classification

Every crystal, oscillator, reset and boot or configuration strap is loaded, referenced and placed as its
device's own documentation requires, and every strap's state at reset is defined by hardware.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | COMPONENT_REQUIREMENT |
| applies | conditional; boards b, c, d, e |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION, EMC, RELIABILITY |

| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** Per oscillator: load capacitance against the crystal's own specification, keep-out and reference under the
loop, and a bounded return path. Per strap: the resistor, the state it sets and the device page that defines
it.

**Why** A mis-loaded crystal and a floating strap are the two defects that make a board 'sometimes work'.

**If violated** Intermittent boot, frequency error, and a clock that radiates.

**Today** crystal loads and straps are chosen in the generators; nothing checks a load capacitance against the crystal,
or a strap's state at reset

| implementation | gen_sch_*.py, with the PCIe clauses of the module datasheet held by check_contracts.py |

**Accept when** A per-interface sheet naming the specification and revision used, the requirement lines taken from it, and
where each is implemented. An interface whose specification is not in the tree is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and says
so.

**Why** The PCIe lanes on board B are assigned to a 90 ohm class because they inherited the USB class, and no PCIe or
M.2 specification is in this tree to say otherwise.

**If violated** A link that does not meet its own specification and cannot be certified.

**Today** 16 September 2026: the FIRST interface source in this tree was read, the Compute Module 5 datasheet, and it
decided three things. PCIe on this host is 90 ohm differential with intra-pair match within 0.1 mm, so the
class board B already assigns is correct and the PCIe wants 85 note of 9 September is withdrawn for this
design. Every PCIe receive line needs a 220 nF series capacitor before it enters the IC, and board B had none
on three slots: six capacitors added at the source and a contract now holds the shape (the module's receive
net carries exactly one capacitor and never a second device). Ethernet is 100 ohm differential, intra-pair
within 0.15 mm. This closes ONE interface of several: USB, M.2 and HDMI have no sheet, which is why the
maturity is GENERATED_ONLY and not ENFORCED

magnetics board B already carries on its wall port

the signal.

**Why** The finish grew into a second router: ten copper-editing passes to close a handful of connections.

**If violated** Every board needs a rescue, and the rescue's own defects are found after the route.

**Today** the principle is written in the record and in the plan; the finish still carries ten copper-editing passes
and the predictor covers two of the classes

pad) is one the chosen process produces, and a via in a pad is declared to the assembler.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | FAB_LIMIT |

| risk | FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, RELIABILITY |

treatment, and the count of vias in pads with the assembly note that accompanies them.

**Why** A via in a pad without a declared treatment is a solder thief the assembler does not expect.

**If violated** Voided joints, open barrels, and a board that passes electrical test and fails in vibration.

anywhere, and several boards carry vias in pads

## Emc

### EMC-001  source, path, victim

For each intentional and unintentional emitter on the board, the coupling path to each susceptible victim is
identified and broken by design: loop area, edge containment, filtering at the boundary, cable treatment and
shielding where they are needed.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, b, c, d, e, p |
| release effect | **MUST_JUSTIFY** |
| risk | EMC, ELECTRICAL_FUNCTION |
| verified by | MANUAL_REVIEW, SIMULATION, PROTOTYPE_MEASUREMENT at ROUTED_BOARD (human or lab only) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | NONE_YET |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | by OWNER, scope the kit, expires pre-compliance testing |

**Accept when** An EMC sheet per board: the switching sources with their frequencies and edge rates, the sensitive victims,
the coupling paths considered, and the measures taken at each; a pre-compliance measurement plan for what
cannot be decided on paper.

**Why** Eleven radios and a sealed metal box make every switching edge somebody's noise floor.

**If violated** Receiver desense in the kit's own box, and a product that cannot pass an emissions test.

**Today** no EMC analysis of any kind exists; eleven radios and a sealed metal box

### REL-001  the build survives its service life

Vibration, shock, flexure, connector mating cycles, moisture, contamination and thermal cycling as the
envelope describes them are considered for every mechanical and electrical interface.

level, and the measure taken (staking, support, strain relief, coating, mating cycle rating).

**Why** A kit that is carried in a vehicle sees more vibration in transport than in use.

**If violated** A tall part shears its joints, a connector wears, a coated board traps moisture.

**Today** nothing considers vibration, mating cycles or moisture for any interface

## Energy Storage

### BAT-001  the cell block is protected in hardware

The cell block has over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, short-circuit and over-temperature protection
in hardware, independent of any software, with the trip points set from the cell manufacturer's own limits.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | REGULATORY |
| applies | conditional; boards p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY |
| verified by | MANUAL_REVIEW, PROTOTYPE_MEASUREMENT, VENDOR_CONFIRMATION at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_sch_p.py BQ4050 and protection FETs |
| maturity | **GENERATED_ONLY** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** Each protection function names the device that implements it, its configured threshold, the cell datasheet
limit it is derived from, and the test that will demonstrate it on the prototype.

**Why** A 200 Wh lithium block is the one part of this kit that can hurt somebody.

**If violated** Thermal runaway from an over-charge, a deep discharge, or an external short.

**Today** the protection is designed and its thresholds are configured in software; no check compares a threshold
against the cell's own limits, and the cell is not chosen

### BAT-002  the energy chain is bounded end to end

From the cells to every load, the maximum fault current is bounded at each stage by a protective element
sized for the conductors and connectors of that stage.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PHYSICS_PRINCIPLE |
| applies | conditional; boards a, e, e5, p |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | SAFETY |
| verified by | CALCULATION, MANUAL_REVIEW at SCHEMATIC (partially automatable) |
| source | SOURCE_UNVERIFIED |
| implementation | gen_sch_a.py, gen_sch_e.py, gen_pcb_e5.py, gen_sch_p.py |
| maturity | **OPEN** |
| owner | OWNER |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** A chain diagram with, at each stage, the conductor and connector rating, the protective element and its
rating, and the prospective fault current.

**Why** Four boards, two blade fuses, a pre-charge pin and 12 AWG wiring are one circuit, not four.

**If violated** A fault in one board is cleared by copper in another.

**Today** the chain crosses four boards with two 25 A blades and 12 AWG wiring, and no document draws it end to end

## Verification Signoff

### SGN-001  every applicable rule has a result

Before any board is released, every rule applicable to it has a result of PASS, WAIVED or NOT_APPLICABLE,
computed from current evidence; absence, staleness or a failed check is INCONCLUSIVE and blocks.

| | |
|---|---|
| classification | PROJECT_DECISION |
| applies | universal for this project |
| release effect | **BLOCKER** |
| risk | DOCUMENTATION, SAFETY |
| verified by | SCRIPT at RELEASE_PACKAGE (automatable) |
| source | NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_PROJECT_DECISION |
| implementation | rules_status.py, over pcb_rules.yaml and pcb_rules_coverage.yaml |
| maturity | **ENFORCED** |
| owner | SESSION |
| waiver | not waivable |

**Accept when** The board's computed status carries a result for every applicable rule, each with its evidence id; the
readiness gate state is reported before any percentage.

**Why** This registry is worth only the computation that reads it.

**If violated** A board is released because nobody asked a question that was never written down.

**Today** 16 September 2026. The verdict read here is rules_complete and NOT rules_status, because the two answer
different questions: rules_status says whether the boards pass, rules_complete says whether every rule that
applies to a board reached one of the five results at all. The second is the property this registry exists
for, and it is the one that would otherwise be invisible, since a rule missing from the table looks exactly
like a rule that does not apply. It is FAIL when any pair produces a result outside the five, when the
registry fails its own validator, or when an applied rule has no coverage entry; 294 of 294 pairs resolve
today
